name: Turbulent Flow Simulation on HPC-Systems
description:
- Introduction to RANS equations for incompressible fluids: concept of RANS and short introduction to turbulence.
- Introduction to programming with C++, numerical discretization of conservation equations, solution methods for incompressible fluids, solution algorithms for differential equations, and visualization of simulation data sets.
- Introduction to parallelization and application of present toolkits.
- Introduction to turbulence modelling, methods for the validation of simulations, investigation of experimental and numerical data sets and their application.
- Introduction to presentation techniques (for example, verbal and non-verbal presentation skills)

At the beginning of the semester, we provide a software package written in C++ that contains basic modules to solve the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. Within two worksheets and the final project, students extend the code with, e.g., a distributed-memory parallelization (MPI) or a turbulence model. These tasks are solved alone during the first worksheet with a weighting factor of 1/6 and then in an interdisciplinary team for the second worksheet with a weighting factor of 3/6 and the final project with a weighting factor of 2/6. The final project is presented to the entire group during a 15-minute presentation in the last lecture. The final grade of this module is determined based on the performance in the worksheets, the final project, and during oral examinations, which are conducted separately or in groups.
prerequisites:
Mechanical Engineering:
- Fundamentals of Numerical Fluid Mechanics (MW0603, MW1913)
- Turbulent Flows (MW0595)
- Fluid mechanics I (MW2021)
- Fluid mechanics II (LRG0071)

Informatics:
- Numerical programming (IN0019) and/or
- Basics of parallel programming (IN2147)
